decision: Implement BRIDGE_MODE as an optional outbound bridge adapter for go_hive. The local process registers an environment with a control plane, long-polls work, acknowledges and heartbeats a lease, maps the work to a real local Hive session, relays permission events, and archives the session. It is v2-style env-less, outbound-only, default off, and post-1.0. It is not a LAN peer transport and it does not claim compatibility with claude.ai or ByteBroad's proprietary bridge until their control-plane contract and OAuth access are provided.
goal_beyond_request: Turn a local go_hive installation into a remotely controlled executor without exposing an inbound port. The remote control plane chooses work; the local process retains ownership of session creation, tool execution, permission decisions and audit. The model never receives a raw remote prompt that bypasses the queen/colony runtime.

feasibility.verdict: 传输可移植；控制面兼容性有条件；产品语义不能照搬。
feasibility.why: Bridge Mode is an outbound long-poll worker protocol, so Go can implement the HTTP client, environment registration, lease, heartbeat, cancellation, session mapping and permission relay with the standard library. The hard dependency is the external control plane: its endpoints, OAuth provider, work result contract and trusted-device semantics are not part of go_hive. A local design can pin a product-owned contract, but cannot honestly claim claude.ai or ByteBroad compatibility without that server contract.
reusable_parts: HTTPS long-poll, bounded backoff and outbound-only networking are straightforward in Go.
hive serve already exposes a real session API: POST /api/sessions, chat, events and DELETE.
hive-cred and the credential store already provide a place for provider credentials; bridge must not invent a plaintext token file.
Sentinel's outbound long-poll listeners are a useful lifecycle and backoff reference, not the bridge protocol itself.
The event bus already carries ask-user and client-input events that can be relayed to a host approval surface.
not_portable: The control-plane endpoints, OAuth refresh and trusted-device rules are external; they cannot be fabricated locally.
A remote work id is not a Hive session id; a mapping and ownership check must be designed, not assumed.
Bridge must not expose an inbound port or reuse HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN.
Bridge is not LAN Pipes: it has no multicast discovery and no peer-to-peer prompt routing.
The feature is outside upstream Hive 1.0 and outside the current alignment scope.

problem.statement: go_hive already has a local session API and a queen/colony runtime, but no outbound control-plane client. An operator who wants to use a web control plane must open an inbound port, copy a desktop token and manually manage sessions. Bridge Mode describes the missing pattern: register once, poll work behind NAT, run a real session, relay approval, and release the lease.
user_value: A local installation can be driven from a control plane without an inbound port.
Remote work maps to a real Hive session, so queen/colony tools and audit still apply.
Permission and ask-user prompts stay human-approved on the host side.
A crashed or stopped worker does not silently duplicate work or leak a lease.
Operators can see environment, work, session and last error in one status surface.
problem.why_not_now: This is an additive remote-control capability, not an upstream Hive feature. It must remain design-only until the control-plane owner, credential model, workspace isolation and permission relay are accepted. A complete-looking page is not implementation evidence.

protocol.name: BRIDGE_MODE
protocol.provider: external control plane (not owned by go_hive; contract unpinned)
protocol.version: v2 env-less preferred; v1 env-based only as a compatibility mode
protocol.transport: outbound HTTPS long-poll (documented 10s timeout); no inbound listener
protocol.auth: OAuth bearer for registration, environment secret for work, trusted-device token for v2
protocol.scope: one private workspace, one active work per environment in v1, post-1.0 optional
protocol.result_contract: not specified by the attached document; must be pinned before implementation

requirements.statement: Keep BRIDGE_MODE opt-in, default off and explicitly post-1.0; no default tool, no always-on listener and no change to the 1.0 parity claim.
requirements.acceptance: With the feature absent/disabled, no bridge client, poller, environment credential, inbound socket or model tool is registered; existing local suites are unchanged.

requirements.statement: Use outbound HTTPS long-poll only. The local process opens no inbound port, does not reuse HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN and does not expose the desktop API to the control plane.
requirements.acceptance: A network probe sees only outbound connections; no bridge listener exists; a control-plane request carrying the desktop token is rejected.

requirements.statement: Pin the control-plane contract before coding: endpoints, version, work payload, result/status channel, error taxonomy and OAuth provider. Unpinned provider behaviour is a blocking external dependency, not a guess.
requirements.acceptance: The design names a concrete control-plane owner/base URL and records the contract version; a fake control plane implements the same schema; an unknown/unsupported version fails closed.

requirements.statement: Store environment secrets and OAuth refresh material in the credential store, never in argv, URLs, logs, plaintext config or the repository; use a dedicated bridge identity, not the desktop token.
requirements.acceptance: Secrets are redacted in logs and errors; config contains a handle/env name only; a missing/expired credential produces a typed error; no token appears in the URL.

requirements.statement: Implement environment lifecycle: register, reuse by id, deregister, and run recovery. Re-registration must be idempotent and must not create a second environment after a crash.
requirements.acceptance: Register returns id/secret; reuse returns the same environment; deregister removes the lease; a crash/restart reuses the persisted id; duplicate registration does not create an orphan.

requirements.statement: Implement work lifecycle with at-most-once side effects: poll, acknowledge, run, heartbeat, stop, archive. Redelivery is deduplicated by work id; ack happens only after local ownership is persisted.
requirements.acceptance: A redelivered work id reuses the existing local session; ack is durable; a duplicate poll does not start a second turn; a lost lease prevents further mutation.

requirements.statement: Map remote work to a real local queen session through a persistent mapping. The remote control plane cannot choose an arbitrary local session, workspace or colony; workspace/profile selection is config-bound.
requirements.acceptance: A work creates or resumes one local session; the mapping survives restart; an unknown remote session id is a typed error; no raw prompt bypasses SessionManager.

requirements.statement: Relay ask-user and tool permission requests to the control plane, but let only the host approve. A remote model cannot self-approve; approval after cancel, timeout, close or lease loss is invalid.
requirements.acceptance: Permission request arrives with work/session/request ids; host approval reaches the session; self-approval is impossible; late/duplicate approval is rejected; no approval UI is model-controlled.

requirements.statement: Define heartbeat and cancellation semantics: lease renewal, soft timeout, hard stop, process crash and control-plane disconnect. A stopped or expired work must not keep running behind the control plane's back.
requirements.acceptance: Heartbeat renews a live lease; stop cancels the local turn; lease expiry stops work; a crash resumes or reports a typed lost-lease error; no zombie session remains.

requirements.statement: Provide a small operator surface: hive bridge status/register/deregister and GET /api/bridge/status. It is host-only and does not add a model-facing bridge tool.
requirements.acceptance: Status shows environment id, control-plane URL, lease, session id, last error and feature state; register/deregister work; the default tool catalogue is unchanged.

requirements.statement: Keep audit and errors compatible with local sessions: environment/work/session ids, permission outcome, stop reason and typed failures are observable without logging tokens or full message bodies.
requirements.acceptance: Audit rows identify the bridge path and outcome; redaction tests pass; a failed work has one typed error and no partial session mutation.

requirements.statement: Respect the package and tool boundary: internal/bridge is independent, a thin server adapter owns session wiring, and no raw protocol method or model-facing bridge tool is registered.
requirements.acceptance: internal/bridge does not import internal/server, internal/cli or internal/tools/builtin; the adapter is the only wiring point; the frozen default tool surface is unchanged.

requirements.statement: Preserve existing local behaviour: no change to desktop auth, session API shapes, stdio channels, queen mail or colony semantics; bridge is additive and scope-checked.
requirements.acceptance: Existing API/session/channel/queen/colony suites pass; bridge-disabled behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged; no new route appears without the feature flag.

requirements.statement: Verify with a fake control plane and a real local session E2E; build with CGO_ENABLED=0; record a real control-plane run as an external gap if no credentials/contract exist.
requirements.acceptance: Fake control-plane tests cover register/poll/ack/heartbeat/stop/archive, crash, duplicate work, permission and redaction; a real session E2E runs; CGO=0 six-platform build passes; external gap is labelled.

non_goals: Do not copy claude.ai or ByteBroad's proprietary control plane or claim compatibility without its contract and OAuth access.
Do not expose an inbound bridge port or reuse HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN as the bridge credential.
Do not add a raw remote prompt path that bypasses SessionManager, queen/colony runtime, permissions or audit.
Do not add LAN discovery, multicast, peer-to-peer control or multi-hop federation; that is the separate LAN Pipes design.
Do not add a model-facing bridge_* tool or a new default tool surface.
Do not add multi-tenant isolation, public internet exposure or a hosted SaaS control plane in v1.
Do not make bridge mode a Hive 1.0 parity item or a commercial release gate without explicit approval.
Do not log environment secrets, OAuth tokens, trusted-device tokens or full message bodies.
assumptions: The control plane owner provides a pinned HTTP contract, OAuth provider and environment registration policy.
The local process has a dedicated workspace and can run without a shared HIVE_HOME containing unrelated sessions.
A remote work is represented by a stable work id and an explicit session reference; unknown types fail closed.
The host UI or CLI is the permission authority; the remote model is never an approval authority.
The control plane can tolerate a 10s long poll, bounded backoff and duplicate deliveries.
A real control-plane run requires credentials not present in this repository and must be recorded separately.
Bridge is single-hop; multi-hop and LAN P2P are separate designs.

options.name: Outbound bridge adapter over the existing Hive session API
options.reason: Keeps session creation, queen/colony semantics, permissions and audit local; works behind NAT; maps cleanly to a v2-style environment and lease.

options.name: Expose the existing hive serve API directly to the control plane
options.reason: Requires an inbound port and broad desktop-token access; the control plane could reach unrelated APIs. It also ignores environment registration, lease and permission relay.

options.name: Reuse LAN Pipes multicast/TCP as the remote control transport
options.reason: Bridge is a control-plane-to-executor direction, not peer discovery. LAN Pipes has no environment registration, lease or remote approval model.

options.name: SSH reverse tunnel or static reverse proxy to hive serve
options.reason: Useful as an emergency deployment, but it provides no environment lifecycle, work queue or remote approval UX and still exposes a broad local API.

options.name: Direct claude.ai / ByteBroad bridge compatibility
options.reason: The endpoints, OAuth, trusted-device and result contract are external and unpinned; claiming compatibility without them would be fabricated.

options.name: In-process delegate_task only
options.reason: It solves local fan-out, not remote control behind NAT. It has no environment, lease, cancellation or control-plane permission semantics.

D1.title: Opt-in scope and deployment
D1.text: Bridge routes and the poller mount only when bridge.enabled is true. Default serve remains loopback; the bridge client is outbound and opens no inbound port. The feature is post-1.0, not part of the frozen route or tool surface, and can be killed without affecting local sessions.

D2.title: Control-plane client contract
D2.text: A single client owns the pinned base URL, API version, OAuth registration, work poll, ack, heartbeat, stop, deregister, archive, permission event and reconnect. It validates server ids with a small allowlist, rejects path traversal, uses bounded timeouts and never reads a per-request URL from work data.

D3.title: Identity and credentials
D3.text: Environment id and secret are issued by registration; OAuth and trusted-device material live in the credential store. Config names a credential handle or env var, never a literal secret. The desktop token is a different principal and is rejected. Logs redact headers, tokens and message bodies.

D4.title: Environment lifecycle
D4.text: Register is idempotent by reuse id; the id/secret pair is persisted atomically before polling. Deregister revokes the lease and stops polling. A restart reuses the persisted environment and does not create an orphan. A failed deregister is reported, not silently ignored.

D5.title: Work lifecycle and idempotency
D5.text: Poll returns one work; the client validates type and required ids, persists a work-to-session mapping, then acks. A redelivered work id reuses that mapping and never starts a second turn. Unknown work types, mismatched environment ids and malformed payloads fail closed before ack.

D6.title: Session mapping and ownership
D6.text: A remote work maps to a local queen session created through the existing SessionManager. The mapping stores environment id, work id, local session id and workspace/profile; it never accepts an arbitrary local session id from the control plane. Colony spawning is allowed through the session's normal runtime and locks the session as usual.

D7.title: Permission relay
D7.text: ask-user and tool-permission events are published to a host approval surface and forwarded as a control-plane event with work, session and request ids. Only a host decision is accepted; request ids expire on cancel, timeout, close or lease loss. A remote model cannot approve its own request.

D8.title: Lease, heartbeat and cancellation
D8.text: A live work renews its lease with heartbeat. Soft timeout asks the session to stop; hard timeout and lease loss cancel the turn. Stop is idempotent and late heartbeats cannot resurrect a lost lease. Process crash recovery either resumes the same session or reports a typed lost-lease error.

D9.title: Events, results and archive
D9.text: Session events are bounded and ordered; the control-plane result channel is pinned before implementation. Archive is idempotent (409 = already archived) and does not delete local audit. An event gap is reported, never silently reset. Local session history remains the durable source.

D10.title: Security and isolation
D10.text: Outbound HTTPS only; control-plane host allowlist; dedicated workspace; no shared HIVE_HOME; no desktop API exposure; no auto-approval; no shell interpolation from remote text; body/event caps; per-environment rate limits; kill switch. The bridge is a remote code-execution surface and is treated as such.

D11.title: Operator surface and audit
D11.text: hive bridge status/register/deregister and GET /api/bridge/status expose enabled, environment id, control-plane URL, lease, work, local session, last error and stop reason. Audit records environment/work/session and permission outcome; tokens and message bodies are redacted.

D12.title: Package, tool and dependency boundary
D12.text: internal/bridge owns transport, protocol, store, lease, runner and policy; internal/server/bridge_adapter.go is the only SessionManager wiring; internal/cli/bridge.go is the operator entry. internal/bridge must not import internal/server, internal/cli or internal/tools/builtin. No model-facing bridge tool is registered; no bundled peer runtime; CGO_ENABLED=0.

config_contract.authority: New optional bridge namespace; do not change desktop auth, channels or queen_mail.

sequence: persist environment id/secret; start outbound poll
poll work; validate environment id and work type
create or resume the local Hive session; run the turn
relay ask-user/tool permission event; host approves or denies
post result/status through the pinned control-plane channel
stop on cancel/lease loss; archive; deregister on shutdown

work_payload.session_id: remote session reference; mapped locally, never trusted as a local id
work_payload.workspace: optional; must match the configured workspace policy
work_payload.expires_at: lease deadline; missing means fail closed

protocol_contract.result_gap: The attached document does not define a result upload endpoint. v1 must pin one (event/result/status) or run without claiming remote result delivery.
protocol_contract.rule: No raw prompt; no arbitrary local route; no per-request control-plane URL; no model self-approval.

limits.max_sessions: v1 default 1; hard cap configurable, never unbounded

limits.archive: 409 is idempotent success; local audit is not deleted
limits.retry: bounded backoff; 401 refresh once; 403/404/410 fatal; no infinite loop

open_questions: Who owns the control plane, and what is the exact pinned API/OAuth/result contract? Without this, implementation is blocked.
Should v1 support only one active work per environment, or a bounded pool? The proposal is one.
Should the remote work map to a queen session or a colony session? The proposal creates a queen session and lets normal colony semantics apply.
What is the result/status channel? The attached document names nine operations but not a result upload; this must be pinned.
Should trusted-device v2 be required, or is environment-secret + TLS sufficient for v1? The proposal prefers v2 when available.
Should bridge mode be in the 1.0 release at all? The proposal keeps it post-1.0 and out of parity.
What is the workspace isolation requirement: dedicated OS user, container, or same-user directory? The proposal requires a dedicated workspace and records OS isolation as an open decision.
